items.requirement: State the research question: Can CNNs generalize across underrepresented colors and train–test hue shifts while retaining color cues that help distinguish classes?
items.quote:
generalize across different colors,
while at the same time also retaining important color information

items.requirement: Explain that CEConvs share input-layer filter weights across discrete hue rotations and preserve hue in a feature-map dimension that shifts with the input hue.
items.quote:
CEConvs share parameters across hue-transformed filters in the input layer and store
color information in hue-equivariant feature maps.

items.requirement: Describe the two ColorMNIST tasks. In the long-tailed task, classes depend on digit identity and color, and the imbalanced training set is evaluated on a balanced test set. In the biased task, varying hue dispersion controls how informative color is about digit identity.

items.requirement: Distinguish classification accuracy on the original test set from mean accuracy across test-time hue shifts spanning −180° to +180°. Label any hue-response curve with test accuracy and shift angle.
items.quote:
the performance on the original test set, as well as the average accuracy

items.requirement: Report that CE-ResNet variants generally maintained comparable original-test accuracy and improved robustness to test-time hue shifts, especially without training jitter. Describe color jitter as complementary and qualify gains by dataset and model variant.
items.quote:
CE-ResNets are also significantly more robust to test-time hue shifts, especially
when trained without color jitter augmentation.
